All error comparisons here refer to acquisition-time forecasts, not current-model residuals.","batch_rationale":"This batch combines direct failure follow-up with experiments that distinguish remaining response relationships across the supplied pool. The m194 panel and m209 singletons address the most consequential new loading-qualified questions. Carbonyl panels test whether recent repairs transfer across conjugation, rigid ring environments, remote ethers, and naphthyl connectivity; m166 tests a particularly unusual forecast dip against matched measured anchors. The ester experiments examine stronger-eluent baselines and recorded nonmonotonic completion shapes, complementing the newly confirmed shallow dodecyl ester and steep naphthyl ester responses. Nitrogen and donor-containing panels fill transitions where endpoint slopes or loading transfer remain unresolved. The paired experiments keep density, sample volume, loading solvent, and loading-solvent volume fixed while changing PE/EA; the m194 middle-loading pair also connects to its measured loading references. Singletons attach to measured anchors rather than opening unrelated grids. No selected pair repeats an identical recorded tuple, and no pending experiment is selected. These labels are intended to improve retrained V1/V2 prediction across repeated structure-condition rows, not to maximize elution volumes or optimize the selected separations. Cross-molecule comparisons remain conditional on injection differences, and the recorded associations do not establish causal loading laws. Loading amount is the supplied density-times-volume feature. CW percentiles and quantile spans only supplement the chemical and observed-data reasoning; quantile spans are not calibrated epistemic uncertainty, and V2 minus V1 is the elution interval width."}
